import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

n = 101
x1 = np.linspace(-3, 3, n)
plt.figure()

g1 = np.power(x1, 3)
g2 = -g1

# Okabe-Ito blue and vermillion (figures/dowling.mplstyle), with distinct
# linestyles and hatches so the two regions stay separable in greyscale.
plt.plot(x1, g1, color="#0072B2", linestyle="-", label=r"$x_2 \leq x_1^3$")
plt.fill_between(
    x1,
    g1,
    np.min(g1) * np.ones(n),
    facecolor="#0072B2",
    edgecolor="#0072B2",
    hatch="//",
    linewidth=0,
    alpha=0.5,
)


plt.plot(x1, g2, color="#D55E00", linestyle="--", label=r"$-x_1^3 \leq x_2$")
plt.fill_between(
    x1,
    np.max(g2) * np.ones(n),
    g2,
    facecolor="#D55E00",
    edgecolor="#D55E00",
    hatch="\\\\",
    linewidth=0,
    alpha=0.5,
)

plt.xlabel("$x_1$")
plt.ylabel("$x_2$")

plt.legend(loc="center left")
plt.show()

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.environ import (
    ConcreteModel,
    Var,
    Objective,
    Constraint,
    SolverFactory,
    Suffix,
    minimize,
    value,
)

## Create concrete Pyomo model
m = ConcreteModel()

## Set up to extract dual variables after model solve.
m.dual = Suffix(direction=Suffix.IMPORT)

## Declare variables with initial values
m.x1 = Var(initialize=1)
m.x2 = Var(initialize=1)

## Declare objective
m.OBJ = Objective(expr=m.x1, sense=minimize)

m.g1 = Constraint(expr=m.x2 <= m.x1**3)

m.g2 = Constraint(expr=-m.x1**3 <= m.x2)

## Specify IPOPT as solver
solver = SolverFactory("ipopt")

## Solve the model
results = solver.solve(m, tee=True)
assert pyo.check_optimal_termination(results), (
    f"Solve failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
    f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
)

## Return the solution
print("x1 = ", value(m.x1))
print("x2 = ", value(m.x2))
print("\n")

## Inspect dual variables
m.dual.display()
